subject: Mythology
title: Temples: Where Gods Live on Earth
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Temples: Where Gods Live on Earth.

hook.text: A Hindu temple is not just a building. It is the body of God, designed so every room represents a divine organ.

buildup.text: The inner sanctum holds the main deity. The tower above it represents the cosmic mountain connecting earth to heaven.

discovery.text: Priests wake, bathe, dress, and feed the deity's statue every day as if the god were physically present.

twist.text: Some temples are so sacred that devotees crawl hundreds of miles on their knees just to reach the entrance.

climax.text: India has over two million temples, making Hinduism the most architecturally expressed religion on the planet.

punchline.text: Two million houses built for gods who the builders believe are actually home.

quiz.question: How do Hindu priests treat the deity statue inside a temple?
options: As a symbolic artwork representing abstract ideas
As if the god were physically present — waking, bathing, and feeding it daily
As a historical artifact preserved behind glass
